evidence_records.claim: Alberta Transportation's RSA Implementation Plan recommends that road safety audits be required as part of the P3 or Design-Build RFP, with the proponent responsible for hiring and administering the road safety audit team as part of the fees.
evidence_records.quote: It is recommended that road safety audits be required as part of the P3 or Design- Build RFP, and it is the proponent’s responsibility to hire and administer the road safety audit team as part of the fees.
evidence_records.source_title: Road Safety Audit Implementation Plan — Final Report (Appendix C: RSA and P3 Delivery Method)
evidence_records.publisher: Alberta Transportation (prepared by G. Ho Engineering Consultants)

evidence_records.claim: The UNB guidelines' highway case study (Appendix C) presents the audit report in tabular format for easy exchange between auditors and client, with three columns: the audit team's observations, suggested possible remediation initiatives, and a space for the client response, returned to the auditors once the client had addressed each issue in writing; this worked example pairs observations with suggested countermeasures even though the body text says reports normally should not contain recommended remedial measures [cf. EV-CA-017].
evidence_records.quote: To facilitate easy exchange of information between auditors and client, the audit report has been prepared in tabular format. There are three columns; the first describing the audit team’s observations, the second suggesting possible remediation initiatives and the third providing a space for the client response. Once the client had addressed each issue on paper, a copy of the document with responses was returned to the auditors.
evidence_records.source_title: Road Safety Audit Guidelines (Appendix C Case Studies — highway case study report format)
evidence_records.publisher: University of New Brunswick Transportation Group

evidence_records.claim: Alberta Transportation's Road Safety Audit Guidelines §5.6.2 requires the project design team to provide a response report to the audit, developed in consultation with the project sponsor, choosing among accept / conditionally-accept-with-modifications / reject — with the reasons for modifications documented; combined with §5.6.1's filing duty ('A copy of the road safety audit report must be made available to Alberta Transportation'), disagreements between audit findings and project records must carry documented reasons rather than standing unexplained.
evidence_records.quote: The project design team must provide a response report to the road safety audit within a reasonable period of time determined in consultation with Alberta Transportation. In preparing the response report, the project team should consult with the project sponsor. Possible responses are: 1. Accept in full and implement changes to project 2. Conditionally accept with modifications. The response report should document the reasons for the modifications 3. Reject with reason
evidence_records.source_title: Alberta Transportation Road Safety Audit Guidelines (§5.6.1–5.6.2 Report and Response Report)
evidence_records.publisher: Alberta Transportation (prepared by G. Ho Engineering Consultants)

evidence_records.claim: The Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual (First Edition, January 2018, Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport) states it 'must be followed by all persons who are involved in the planning, design or construction of changes to the Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Network (EADRN)' and by those commissioned to undertake the audits.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clause 1.2.1-1.2.2
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT) / Abu Dhabi Municipality e-library

evidence_records.claim: The Abu Dhabi manual combines existing practice of Abu Dhabi Municipality and the Department of Transport, which previously compiled best international practice from Europe, Australia, New Zealand and the Middle East (Dubai).
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clause 1.3.1
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: The Abu Dhabi manual's procedures are stated to be based largely on the UK Highways Agency's and Transport Infrastructure Ireland's HD 19/15 procedures, with additional requirements specific to Abu Dhabi.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clause 5.1.1
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Abu Dhabi defines a native 'Stage 0 – Feasibility Road Safety Audit': an early-design-stage RSA used to define high-level safety choices of alignment, transport or development plans, to pre-empt countermeasures, and to help select a preferred option where more than one exists; all small private developments should be assessed by the highway authority's road safety audit team at conception, and a Stage 0 audit is required where it will assist in defining design choices.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, definition 2.1.29
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Stage 0 audits shall be undertaken during feasibility/conceptual design on each probable route or option for large-scale developments, route realignments, new major inter-urban links and major transport developments; a Stage 0 RSA must accompany any Master Plan and TIS identified by the road authority's road safety team as requiring one, and a Stage 0 must also be considered at concept stage for all private developments, with exemptions available from the road authority's road safety team.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clauses 4.2.1-4.2.4
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Abu Dhabi Stage 1 (Preliminary Design RSA) shall be undertaken near to but prior to completion of preliminary design, finalised before commitment to construct or land purchase, with drawings typically limited to general details (route alignment, profile, typical cross-sections) and a mandatory joint site visit to assess tie-ins and consistency for all road users.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, definition 2.1.30 and clauses 4.3.1-4.3.7
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Abu Dhabi Stage 2 (Detailed Design RSA) shall be undertaken at completion of detailed design but before tender or construction commences; tender/contract documents should provide for the contractor to employ a road-authority-approved RSA team, and Design-Build / Design-Build-Operate contracts should engage an approved RSA team for interim RSAs of final designs as they evolve.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, definition 2.1.31 and clause 4.4.1
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Abu Dhabi Stage 3 (Construction/Opening RSA) is undertaken at substantial completion preferably before opening to traffic (Pre-Opening Stage 3a); where pre-opening audit is not feasible it can be completed as a phased or complete opening audit (Stage 3b) within two weeks of opening but before handover; the Stage 3 is essentially a site visit attended by all team members in daylight and darkness, and police should be invited to attend.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, definition 2.1.32 and clauses 4.5.1-4.5.5
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Abu Dhabi Stage 4 comprises data-driven post-opening investigations at the 12-month (Stage 4a) and 36-month (Stage 4b) anniversaries using crash data supplied by Abu Dhabi Police (which, with SAAED, are the sole collision-data recording agencies in Abu Dhabi); the decision to undertake Stage 4 is determined by post-opening crash history, and where no crashes occurred an audit is not required but a note to that effect must be generated by the relevant road authority.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, definition 2.1.33 and clauses 4.6.1-4.6.7
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: It is mandatory to undertake the full range of audits — Stage 0, Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3, and Stage 4 monitoring at 12 and 36 months — for all new major transport or road projects in Abu Dhabi.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clause 5.3.1
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: All road and transport projects in Abu Dhabi must be audited at design and construction stages, but the Feasibility (Stage 0) and/or Preliminary (Stage 1) design stage audits may be exempted where the project is of a scale deemed not to warrant either one or both of those stages, with exemption approval obtained early in the design process from the relevant roads authority and recorded in the design file.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clauses 5.3.2-5.3.3
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Where an Abu Dhabi project is of a scale that no feasibility or preliminary design stage audit was necessary and it progresses directly to detailed design, Audit Stages 1 and 2 can be combined at Stage 2 and referred to as a 'Stage 1/2' single audit report (the manual also states generally that for smaller schemes Stage 1 and Stage 2 can be combined into a single RSA report), with the road authority consulted on which stages shall be undertaken.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clause 5.3.4 and clause 4.1.2
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Appendix A of the Abu Dhabi manual maps scheme types to permitted audit-stage combinations — major new/route-selection projects get the full set (Stages 0, 1, 2, 3, 4); on-line rehabilitations and street-furniture additions skip Stage 0; medium works run Stage 2/3/4 exempted from Stage 1; minor private developments and minor rehabilitations reduce to a combined Stage 1/2 plus Stage 3 or even 'RSA Feedback Form Only'; complex work-zone traffic management gets a WZTTM audit with feedback form only; and like-for-like maintenance is EXEMPT.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, Appendix A: Scheme Type and Road Safety Audit Stage
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: The Abu Dhabi RSA Exemption Note/Certificate (required where indicated on the Appendix A table) enumerates six disposition categories: deferred to next design stage (Stage 0 and/or Stage 1 only); minor works with minimal design approved for a Stage 1/2 RSA at detailed design; exempt as minor works of negligible effect on the EADRN; exempt as like-for-like replacement maintenance; exempt as refurbishment of existing street furniture; or exempt for another described reason — signed by the designer and approved by the Roads Authority road safety team, with a copy kept in the design file.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, Appendix C: Sample RSA Exemption Note/Certificate
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: An Abu Dhabi RSA team shall comprise no less than two persons (Audit Team Leader plus Audit Team Member); the Leader must demonstrate 5 years (2 for Al Ain/Al Dhafra region municipalities per the manual's ATM allowance) of safety engineering/crash analysis/collision investigation, a 10-day recognised collision-investigation or road-safety-engineering course, at least 5 RSAs in the past 12 months as Leader or Member, 2 days CPD in the past 12 months, and well-rounded highway design knowledge; the Member needs 2 years experience, the same 10-day course, 5 RSAs in the past 24 months as Member/Observer and CPD; auditors who audit full time to the exclusion of other road-safety work are unacceptable.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clauses 3.2.1, 3.2.4, 3.3.1, 3.4.1, 3.5.1
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: In Abu Dhabi the RSA team is appointed only with the approval of the relevant roads authority, which assesses competence, independence and current registration; approvals are project- and stage-specific; an RSA submitted with an unapproved team will be rejected; Audit Team Observers are normally limited to two; Specialist Advisors advise but are not team members; the team must have had no connection with the design being audited; and the same team is not required across all stages.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clauses 3.2.3, 5.5.1-5.5.10, 5.6.1
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Abu Dhabi audits carry explicit shelf-life rules: an audit is void and must be redone if not completed (designer responses reviewed by the auditor and received by the roads authority) within 6 months; completed Stage 1, combined Stage 1/2 and Stage 2 audits must be repeated if the design materially changes or the previous audit is more than 2 years old (Stage 0 may extend to 5 years); and the roads authority may extend shelf-life at its discretion up to a maximum of four years.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clauses 5.4.1-5.4.3
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Every Abu Dhabi audit stage requires at least a daytime site visit by all team members together, and a night-time site visit is additionally mandatory at all Stage 3 and Stage 4 audits and all Road Safety Inspections, with exemptions from day- or night-time visits possible only for very minor works at the discretion of the road authority's road safety section.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clauses 5.12.1-5.12.2
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Abu Dhabi output/response obligations: the Stage 0/1/2/3 report follows a fixed content list (scheme description, stage and team identification, site visit record, problems with reasoning, marked-up map/photos, signed team statement, document list, per-problem statement of location/nature/likely crash types, per-problem recommendation); the highway authority gets the draft for comment within 7 working days; the finished report goes simultaneously to client, designer/contractor and roads authority (plus Police at Stages 3/4); the designer/client must respond formally via the feedback/exception form giving reasons and alternatives for any rejected recommendation; the auditor reviews responses; the roads authority finalises and signs the exemption report, which completes the RSA process — a design stage remains 'incomplete' until the exception report is authorised; and Abu Dhabi Police and the roads authority reserve the right to reject any audit or exception report where road safety would be compromised.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clauses 5.13.2-5.13.5, 5.14.1-5.14.6, 5.15.1-5.15.3, 5.16.3
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Abu Dhabi risk semantics are qualitative: each finding must state the location, nature, and the type of crashes considered likely to result (the specimen report uses types such as side-swipe, rear shunt, overshoot and collisions with non-motorised users), recommendations are advisory ('the auditor cannot give instructions') and must be proportionate and viable, 'monitor' recommendations are restricted to identified manoeuvres or causation factors with a named owner, and the manual defines no numeric severity/probability scoring matrix.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, clauses 5.13.2(h)-(j) and Appendix E example report
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: Interim Road Safety Audits in Abu Dhabi may be applied at any time during preliminary and construction stages at the Client's discretion, but are explicitly not mandatory and not a substitute for the formal Stage 1, 2 and 3 Safety Audits, and Design Teams may not contact Audit Teams without the Client's prior written authorisation.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, definition 2.1.18 and clauses 4.7.1-4.7.2
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipal Affairs and Transport

evidence_records.claim: TR-540 is the QCC-published technical reference for the Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, described by QCC's infrastructure standards list as a compiled set of RSA rules and policies standardising infrastructure stages in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, serving as the official reference for all road safety audit activities in the Emirate (covering pre-design and design activities, monitoring, and post-construction site inspection), with a current amendment adding detail on auditor training/experience, audit stages and procedure.
evidence_records.source_title: EMIRATE OF ABU DHABI ROAD SAFETY AUDIT MANUAL (QCC ISGL list, TR-540)
evidence_records.publisher: Abu Dhabi Quality and Conformity Council (QCC)

evidence_records.claim: As of May 2025 the Integrated Transport Centre (ITC) of Abu Dhabi was preparing an update of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual (TR-540) integrating the Safe Systems Approach under Vision Zero, including a structured quantitative risk matrix assessing exposure, likelihood and severity against human injury tolerance, and a move to team-based auditor approvals.
evidence_records.source_title: CIHT UAE Seminar Bulletin — Road Safety Audit: TR-540 Manual Update & Common RSA Problems (13 May 2025)
evidence_records.publisher: Chartered Institution of Highways & Transportation (CIHT) UAE group

evidence_records.claim: Abu Dhabi's ITC traffic-detour permit regime operationally enforces the RSA process: authorised parties must act in accordance with approved manuals including the Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual, and closing out a detour permit requires Road Safety Audit (Stage 3) approval from the respective municipality plus a client letter confirming all comments identified in the RSA report are addressed.
evidence_records.source_title: Procedures Manual for the Implementation of the Regulatory Bylaw of Traffic Detours in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi (Article 6; permit close-out requirements)
evidence_records.publisher: Integrated Transport Centre (ITC) of the Department of Municipalities and Transport

evidence_records.claim: A distinct 'Dubai Road Safety Audit Manual' exists as Dubai's emirate-level RSA standard alongside Abu Dhabi's TR-540 (both named as the relevant UAE standards by CIHT UAE practitioners, and a 110-page document of that title circulates on Scribd), but no official RTA-hosted copy was accessible, so its stage model, team rules and outputs could not be verified.
evidence_records.source_title: CIHT Dubai Evening Seminar Bulletin — Planning, Executing and Responding to Road Safety Audits (7 July 2020)
evidence_records.publisher: Chartered Institution of Highways & Transportation (CIHT) Dubai group

evidence_records.claim: Practitioners presenting under CIHT UAE stated there are currently no legal implications known in the UAE for ignoring road safety audit recommendations, though schemes may ultimately fail approval by the highway authorities — contrasting with the UK where ignoring recommendations carries legal consequences.
evidence_records.source_title: CIHT Dubai Evening Seminar Bulletin — Q&A (7 July 2020)
evidence_records.publisher: Chartered Institution of Highways & Transportation (CIHT) Dubai group

evidence_records.claim: Practitioner discussion at the May 2025 CIHT UAE seminar identified TR-531 as the Abu Dhabi Temporary Traffic Management Manual and acknowledged that many temporary traffic management schemes in Al Ain and greater Abu Dhabi lack required TTM audits, a coverage gap the TR-540 update aims to address.
evidence_records.source_title: CIHT UAE Seminar Bulletin — Q&A on TTM audits and TR-531 (13 May 2025)
evidence_records.publisher: Chartered Institution of Highways & Transportation (CIHT) UAE group

evidence_records.claim: Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority conducted a comprehensive road safety audit of approximately 1,000 km of its existing road network in 2019 as a systematic check of safety deficiencies, reporting 3,823 injury crashes on those roads over 2014-2018 — demonstrating RTA practice of auditing existing roads rather than only new schemes.
evidence_records.source_title: Dubai Auditing of Existing Roads — Safer Roads award entry (2022)
evidence_records.publisher: Road Safety Awards (Loughborough University / Highways Industry partnership programme)

evidence_records.claim: The TR-540 Second Edition scope clause binds all persons involved in the planning, design or construction of changes to the Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Network (EADRN) — and those commissioned to undertake audits — to follow the manual so that the road safety implications of all projects are fully considered for all road users and others affected by the project; verified verbatim from the full QCC-hosted PDF (previously only search-engine excerpts existed, see [EV-AE-022]).
evidence_records.quote: This manual must be followed by all persons who are involved in the planning, design or construction of changes to the Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Network (EADRN) and those who are commissioned to undertake audits to ensure that the road safety implications of all projects are fully considered for all road users and others affected by the project.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual (TR-540, Second Edition), Section 5 “Scope of this Manual” (PDF p. 7)
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT) / Quality and Conformity Council (QCC), Government of Abu Dhabi

evidence_records.claim: TR-540 Second Edition defines native Stage 0 verbatim as a feasibility-stage RSA used to assist in defining high-level road safety choices of road alignment, transport or development plans, identifying possible safety problems to pre-empt countermeasures early and helping identify the preferred option where more than one design option exists — substantiating Abu Dhabi Stage 0 = feasibility/conceptual from the current framework document itself.
evidence_records.quote: A feasibility stage RSA is an early design stage RSA used to assist in defining the high-level road safety choices of road alignment, transport or development plans or developments. It is used to identify possible safety problems likely to impact on a project and pre -empt counter measures at an early stage. Where more than one design option exists, the Road Safety Audit may help to identify the preferred option.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual (TR-540, Second Edition), Section 7 Definitions, item 28 “Stage 0 – Feasibility, Road Safety Audit” (PDF p. 9)
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT) / Quality and Conformity Council (QCC), Government of Abu Dhabi

evidence_records.claim: TR-540 Second Edition permits combining Audit Stages 1 and 2 at Stage 2 as a “Stage 1 / 2” audit where no feasibility or preliminary design stage audit was necessary and the project progressed directly to detailed design, with the relevant road authority consulted on the audit stages to be undertaken; it separately states that for smaller schemes stage 1 and stage 2 can be combined into a single road safety audit report (“RSA Stage 1 / 2”) after getting the approval from the authority (PDF p. 13).
evidence_records.quote: Where a project is of a scale that no feasibility or preliminary design stage audit has been necessary and the project has progressed directly to detailed design, Audit Stages 1 and 2 can be combined at Stage 2 and referred to as a Stage 1 / 2. The relevant road authority should be consulted on the audit stages that shall be undertaken.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual (TR-540, Second Edition), Section 9 Audit Stages (PDF p. 21)
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT) / Quality and Conformity Council (QCC), Government of Abu Dhabi

evidence_records.claim: TR-540 Second Edition makes auditor independence central to the procedures: no member of the Audit Team may have had any connection with the design of the measures being audited, and that independence must be maintained throughout the audit process (direct contact with the Design Team remains permitted, e.g. for clarifying the Audit Brief).
evidence_records.quote: It is central to the auditing procedures that no member of the Audit Team has had any connection with the design of the measures being audited and should maintain this independence throughout the audit process.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual (TR-540, Second Edition), Section 10 Road Safety Audit Procedure, “Independence of the Road Safety Audit Team” (PDF p. 22)
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT) / Quality and Conformity Council (QCC), Government of Abu Dhabi

evidence_records.claim: In UAE practice the designer's formal reply is termed the Design Team Response (DTR): it notes the issues identified and recommendations made, proposes actions in response and advises the scheme's Client on next steps; the DTR is for the Client rather than the Audit Team, and the Client makes the final decision on the way forward — resolving the acronym behind the manual's response/exception machinery (whose Appendix C artifact is titled “RSA Decision Tracking Form”).
evidence_records.quote: The Design Team Response (DTR) should note the issues identified and recommendations made, propose actions in response and advise the Client to the scheme on next steps. The DTR is supposed to be for the Client, not the Audit Team, and the Client should make the final decision on the way forward.
evidence_records.source_title: CIHT Dubai Evening Seminar Bulletin — Planning, Executing and Responding to Road Safety Audits, DTR workflow description (7 July 2020), p. 2
evidence_records.publisher: Chartered Institution of Highways & Transportation (CIHT) Dubai group (non-official bulletin)

evidence_records.claim: At Stage 3 RSA, TR-540 requires the road safety auditor to be aware of issues impacting all road users including the continuity of pedestrian, cycle, mobility-impaired, micromobility (“micro mobility”) and other vulnerable road user accesses and facilities, and directs reference to an Interim Advice Note on Vulnerable Road Users — VRU provisions embedded directly in the audit workflow.
evidence_records.quote: It is essential at the Stage 3 RSA that the road safety auditor is aware of issues that may impact on all road users including the continuity of pedestrian, cycle, mobility impaired, micro mobility users and other vulnerable road user accesses and facilities. Reference should be made to the Interim Advice Note on Vulnerable Road Users.
evidence_records.source_title: Emirate of Abu Dhabi Road Safety Audit Manual (TR-540, Second Edition), Section 9 Audit Stages, Stage 3 site-attendance guidance (PDF p. 16)
evidence_records.publisher: Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT) / Quality and Conformity Council (QCC), Government of Abu Dhabi

evidence_records.claim: TR-514 §2.13 hard-wires TR-540 into the geometric-design workflow: designers must ensure all schemes undergo the relevant pre-construction stage audits — Conceptual Design (Stage 0), Preliminary Design (Stage 1), Detailed Design (Stage 2) — considering safety requirements for ALL road users, with each stage audit closed by the relevant Abu Dhabi Transport Infrastructure authority before progressing to the next design stage or before “Issued for Construction” (IFC) drawings are issued; all pedestrian and cycling facility improvements are subject to RSA conducted by an independent third party from the design team. (Original spelling “Conctruction” preserved.)
evidence_records.quote: Designers to ensure that all schemes to undergo relevant stage audits as per requirements set out in the Road Safety Audit Manual TR-540; designers to ensure consideration of safety requirements for ALL Road users. The following Pre-Construction Audits to be undertaken: Conceptual Design Stage Audits (Stage 0) Preliminary Design Stage Audits (Stage 1) Detailed Design Stage Audit (Stage 2) The above stage audits must be closed by the relevant Abu Dhabi Transport Infrastructure authority to move to the next stage of Design or before “Issued for Conctruction” (IFC) Drawings are issued. All pedestrian and cycling facilities improvements are subject to RSA in accordance with TR -540. RSA to be conducted by an independent 3rd party from the design team.

evidence_records.claim: Per the TR-540 update co-author speaking at the May 2025 CIHT UAE seminar, under the forthcoming standard risk will be assessed on Safe System principles such that if a pedestrian can be hit at 30 km/h or above it is a problem, and pedestrians, junctions and roads at prevailing high UAE speed limits do not comply with the Safe Systems Approach — concretising the quantitative-risk direction flagged in [EV-AE-023] and predicting audit conflict over speed.
evidence_records.quote: Under the new Road Safety Audit standard, risk is assessed based on the Safe Systems and if a pedestrian can be hit at 30 kph or above it is a problem. As I alluded to earlier, pedestrians, junctions and roads at our high-speed limits do not comply with the Safe Systems Approach.
evidence_records.source_title: CIHT UAE Seminar Bulletin — Road Safety Audit: TR-540 Manual Update & Common RSA Problems, Q&A on Safe Systems risk thresholds (13 May 2025), p. 3
